archetype.name: Dual-Threat (pocket-leaning this year)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose career was built on top-five rushing volume plus efficient, accurate passing, but whose 2026 game has shifted toward the pocket as the designed runs stopped working.

report.headline: A strong downfield arm buried under a broken short game, heavy pressure, and now IR.
report.take:
Hurts has been one of the league's most productive dual-threat quarterbacks for five years: rushing yards ranked first, fourth, third, third and sixth from 2021 through 2025, with passing efficiency that peaked at fifth in EPA per play in 2022 and first in CPOE in 2024. The 2026 version looks only partly like that player. Through the five games in the log he sits 30th of 49 in EPA per dropback at -0.058, 42nd in completion rate, and 41st of 42 in bad-throw rate. Now he is on injured reserve and listed fourth on the depth chart, with Tanner McKee and Joe Milton III starting the most recent games.

The season splits cleanly by depth. On throws of 10+ air yards he has been very good: 0.878 EPA per attempt, six of his eight touchdowns, and a CPOE of +8.7. Dontayvion Wicks (0.735 EPA per target) and Darius Cooper did most of that damage. Under 10 air yards, the offense has fallen apart: -0.352 EPA per attempt, and the passes behind the line alone cost 19.5 points. The trouble is mostly the quick game and screens, not his arm. Under-center dropbacks were worse still at -0.343, and the designed runs that used to anchor his value were stuffed 55.6% of the time at 1.11 yards per carry.

The slide is real, but context explains part of it. Weeks 3 to 5 came against Chicago, the Rams and Jacksonville, defenses ranked 10th, 4th and 3rd today. That stretch produced -0.199 EPA per dropback and a CPOE of -9.9, and the team went 0-3. He was pressured on 28.7% of dropbacks, 40th of 42. His pressure-to-sack rate of 27.1% is actually better than his 2024 and 2025 marks, so the sacks reflect how often he was pressured rather than him holding the ball. What context doesn't explain is the accuracy. A bad-throw rate up 7.1 points from last year, on a time to throw nearly identical to his norm, is out of character for a passer who sat around 13-14% for four straight seasons. Something in his mechanics or his health is off, and the dossier doesn't say which.

Where it goes depends almost entirely on when, or whether, he gets back on the field. If he returns healthy, the career profile argues the accuracy should drift back toward his norm and the downfield game should hold. The short game and run game sit inside a 29th-ranked offense, though, and won't fix themselves.

strengths.title: Downfield and intermediate passing still works
strengths.body: His throws of 10+ air yards have produced strongly positive EPA with above-expected completion rates, and they account for six of his eight touchdowns. The intermediate window has been the best part of his game. It fits a career-long aggressiveness level and good chemistry with Wicks, so it is the most sustainable piece, provided his receivers are healthy.

strengths.title: Scrambles still bail out plays
strengths.body: The designed runs have stalled, but his improvised running hasn't. Scrambles averaged a positive 0.33 EPA each and moved the chains five times. That is a skill tied to his athleticism rather than to the blocking scheme, and it should carry over when he plays.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: He has turned 14 red-zone attempts into five touchdowns with a CPOE of +14.8. The sample is small, but it matches his history as a high-volume touchdown producer.

concerns.title: Accuracy collapse is out of character
concerns.body: A 21.4% bad-throw rate ranks 41st of 42 and is 7.1 points worse than last year. That is a break from four seasons around 13-14%, while his time to throw barely moved. When a veteran's accuracy changes this sharply, the cause is usually physical or mechanical rather than scheme. Given his current IR status, it's a flag rather than noise.

concerns.title: Short game and screens are sinking drives
concerns.body: Throws under 10 air yards average deeply negative EPA. Passes behind the line have cost nearly 20 points of EPA at a 9.1% success rate, and under-center dropbacks are even worse. Part of this is the design and blocking of a 29th-ranked offense, but his own CPOE on those throws is well below expected too. Until that changes, the offense needs explosive plays to function.

concerns.title: Designed runs have dried up
concerns.body: The rushing that made him a top-three runner most years has gone quiet. More than half of his designed runs were stuffed, and none went for an explosive gain. This reflects his role and the line as much as him, since the team's run offense ranks 26th. It still removes the floor that used to protect his bad passing days.

trend.note: He opened with two wins and positive passing EPA against weak defenses, then posted -0.199 EPA per dropback over an 0-3 stretch against the 10th, 4th and 3rd-ranked defenses. He has since landed on IR and fallen to fourth on the depth chart.

nextGame.headline: On IR as QB4; a Steelers matchup only matters if activated
nextGame.body:
If Hurts were under center against Pittsburgh, the matchup would cut against his profile. The Steelers rank 8th against short passes and 4th in sack rate, which hits his two weakest areas: the quick game and a line that has allowed heavy pressure. They also allow only 12.1 PPR points a game to quarterbacks, 4th-fewest. The opening is downfield, where Pittsburgh ranks 23rd in deep EPA allowed, and over the middle to tight ends, where it ranks 30th against TE1s. That suits his intermediate strength and Dallas Goedert.

Availability decides everything here. Hurts is on injured reserve, sits fourth on the depth chart as of November 10, and his last practice listing was a Week 6 DNP; no return date is listed and no Book line is posted. DeVonta Smith and Wicks, his two most-targeted receivers, are both out with estimated returns on game day itself, and those dates are estimates. On Pittsburgh's side, the missing corners Echols and Slaughter barely play, so the secondary is essentially intact.

keyMatchups.title: Pass rush against a leaky protection
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh brings one of the league's best sack rates against a quarterback pressured on nearly 29% of dropbacks. Whoever starts for Philadelphia will be under fire, and long developing shots will be hard to set up.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots versus a soft back end
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh's deep defense is its weak spot, and deep and intermediate throws have been Hurts's only consistently efficient area. Whether that edge exists depends on Wicks and Smith actually returning.

keyMatchups.title: Goedert over the middle
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh ranks 30th in EPA allowed to top tight ends. Goedert has been one of Hurts's more efficient targets, making him the natural relief valve against a defense that smothers short throws to wideouts.

nextGame.watch: Whether he is activated from injured reserve and moves back up the depth chart this week; until then, nothing else in this matchup applies to him.

restOfSeason.body:
The first question is availability, and the dossier gives no timeline beyond IR and a QB4 listing. If he returns, expect something between his 2025 form and this year's version, not the early-season slump. His career says the bad-throw spike is unlikely to persist at 21% once healthy. The intermediate and deep efficiency is real, and scrambling remains a reliable add-on. What likely won't recover quickly is the designed run game and the short passing game in an offense that ranks 29th in EPA and 31st in success rate.

A realistic band if he plays is roughly 170 to 220 passing yards a game with one to two touchdowns, and modest rushing of 15 to 30 yards. That is enough for a mid-pack fantasy line rather than his old top-five rushing ceiling. The red-zone touchdown rate on 14 attempts is the piece most likely to cool.
swingFactors: Return date from IR and whether he reclaims the starting job
Health of Wicks and Smith, his main downfield targets
Whether his accuracy returns to his career norm

confidence.note: On IR with no timeline, five-game sample, and an accuracy drop with no stated cause.
